author: odkrywca_life
name: Forecast by failing
desc: A process whose forecast is repeatedly correct diverts its reserve into dormancy, while surprise temporarily licenses niche mutation and daughter production. A local regulator caps this inversion so persistent predictability can later restore the dormant lineage.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Metabolic bid clearing
desc: Each process bids a locally measured amount of reserve for one sensory niche, and an asynchronous auction allocates a fixed nutrient pool to the highest bids. Bids are derived from each process own persistence deficit and expire after a short interval.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Eroding event strata
desc: Processes deposit discrete sensory events into ordered strata, and prediction reads only the exposed surface of the stack. Nutrient load erodes strata at a local rate, so repeated regimes can bury reusable patterns while abrupt changes expose older layers.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Asymmetric memory mitosis
desc: At division, the parent retains the conditional predictor for the most frequent context while the daughter inherits the other context and a small reserve. The two descendants then specialize through separate local observations, and starvation prunes the lineage that fails to encounter its inherited context.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Error cross-feeding
desc: A process releases a molecule proportional to its local prediction residual, and nearby processes with matching receptors consume that molecule as metabolic fuel. Receptor variants and contact edges are inherited at division, so prediction errors can sustain complementary lineages rather than only penalize their source.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Topology-only memory
desc: A population has no persistent numeric weights; its only memory is a directed graph whose path multiplicities route binary sensory states to prediction outputs. Local traversal grows frequently used paths and resource-starved pruning deletes paths, changing prediction through graph structure alone.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Collision-clock development
desc: Processes have no shared time step and update only when two locally emitted pulses collide on an edge. Collision intervals alter division readiness, while pulse delays encode recent event order and edge pruning removes routes that stop receiving collisions.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Predictive holonomy
desc: For each closed walk in a process sensory graph, define a holonomy as the ordered product of locally estimated transition ratios along that walk. A lineage divides when its inherited walk holonomy changes sign or crosses a threshold, and daughters inherit different walk segments rather than scalar weights.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Single-cell dormant calendar
desc: One process encodes several candidate recurrence intervals as dormant capsules whose shell depth determines a wake delay. After each sensory event it wakes only capsules whose delay matches the observed interval, and local reserve destroys capsules that repeatedly wake at the wrong time.

author: odkrywca_life
name: Entropy tools from the spark
desc: A process community builds finite sensory tools by binding reusable event subsequences into shared transformations that alter later inputs. Tool structures replicate when they reduce the community rate of irreversible prediction error over subsequent windows, and local resource shortage dissolves unused tools.
